reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess whether the adoptively transferred CD8+ T cells successfully engaged melanoma antigens. The trial was terminated early due to withdrawal of CRADA partner with only 3 patients enrolled. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No evidence provided about downstream immune activation or T cell expansion/persistence following adoptive transfer. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint failed - only 1/3 patients achieved partial response (33% response rate), with 2/3 showing progressive disease. This is below typical thresholds for clinical activity in melanoma. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: With only 3 patients total, no meaningful subgroup analysis is possible. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Major confounders include severely underpowered study (N=3 vs typical Phase 2 requirements of 15-30+ patients), early termination for non-scientific reasons, and lack of any biomarker readouts to assess mechanism engagement.
